'''''Roemeria argemone''''' (syn. ''Papaver argemone'') is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the poppy family [[Papaveraceae]]. Its common names include '''long pricklyhead poppy''', '''prickly poppy''' and '''pale poppy'''. Its native range includes parts of [[Eurasia]] and [[North Africa]], but it can be found growing wild in parts of North America, where it is an [[introduced species]]. It is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].

==Description==
This [[annual plant]] grows up to {{cvt|50|cm}},<ref name="eflora">{{cite web |title=FNA Vol. 3 |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=233500841 |publisher=efloras.org ([[Flora of North America]]) |accessdate=1 November 2017}}</ref> Its {{cvt|15|-|50|cm|0}} long, branching stems are coated in stiff prickly hairs.<ref name=Readers>{{cite book |year=1981 |title=Reader's Digest Field Guide to the Wild Flowers of Britain |page=31 |publisher=[[Reader's Digest]] |isbn=9780276002175}}</ref> The fern-like green, leaves at the base of the plant have stalks, but upper leaves are stalk-less. They can be up to {{cvt|20|cm|0}} long,<ref name="eflora"/> It blooms in spring to summer,<ref name="eflora"/> between May and July.<ref name=Readers/> The flowers have four slightly overlapping red petals, each with a dark base.<ref name=Readers/> They can measure {{cvt|2|-|5.5|cm|1}} across,<ref name=Readers/> with pale blue [[anthers]] and 4-6 stigmas.<ref name="eflora"/> Later, the plant produces a seed capsule, oblong to clavate (shaped like a club) with ribs and up to 2 cm long.<ref name="eflora"/><ref name=Readers/>

===Biochemistry===
The plant contains [[alkaloids]] and has been used in herbal medicines. It also means the plant is not eaten much by grazing animals.<ref name=Readers/>

==Taxonomy==
[[File:Illustration Papaver argemone0.jpg|thumb|Illustration from Prof. Dr. Otto Wilhelm Thomé's book {{Lang|de|Flora von Deutschland}} in 1885]]
It is commonly known as 'prickly poppy', 'pale poppy',<ref name="rhs">{{cite web |title=''Papaver argemone'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/59432/Papaver-argemone/Details? |publisher=rhs.org.uk |accessdate=1 November 2017}}</ref><ref name="grin">{{cite web |title=Taxon: ''Papaver argemone'' L. |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=26668 |publisher=ars-grin.gov |accessdate=1 November 2017}}</ref> and 'long pricklyhead poppy'.<ref name="catalogueoflife"/><ref>Robert E. Gough and Cheryl Moore-Gough {{google books |EuQ4eWtUGlwC|The Complete Guide to Saving Seeds: 322 Vegetables, Herbs, Fruits, Flowers Trees and Shrubs |page=206}}</ref> It is known as {{Lang|de|Sand-Mohn}} in [[German language|German]], {{Lang|sv|spikvallmo}} in [[Swedish language|Swedish]],<ref name="grin"/> and {{Lang|es|amapola macho}} in [[Spanish language|Spanish]].<ref name="catalogueoflife"/>

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''argemone'' is derived from the [[Greek language|Greek]] 'argema' meaning cataract, and was applied by [[Pedanius Dioscorides|Dioscorides]] to a poppy-like plant used to treat [[cataract]]s.<ref>Archibald William Smith {{google books |ahNMkgoNJ7IC|A Gardener's Handbook of Plant Names: Their Meanings and Origins |page=43}}</ref> See ''[[Argemone]]'' (a genus of flowering plants in the family Papaveraceae commonly known as 'prickly poppies').

It was [[Species description|formally described]] by the Swedish botanist [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his seminal publication ''Species Plantarum'' in 1753 on page 506.<ref name="plantlist"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Papaveraceae ''Papaver argemone'' L. |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=305858-2 |publisher=ipni.org |accessdate=1 November 2017}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is [[native plant|native]] to temperate regions of North Africa, Europe and Western Asia.<ref name="eflora"/><ref name="grin"/> including [[Macaronesia]], [[Canary Islands]], [[Algeria]], [[Egypt]] and [[Morocco]]. Within Western Asia it is found in the Caucasus, [[Armenia]], [[Cyprus]], [[Egypt]] (in the [[Sinai Peninsula|Sinai]]), [[Iran]], [[Iraq]], [[Israel]], [[Jordan]], [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]] and [[Turkey]]. In eastern Europe, it is found within [[Belarus]], [[Estonia]], [[Latvia]], [[Lithuania]], [[Moldova]] and [[Ukraine]]. In middle Europe, it is in [[Austria]], [[Belgium]], [[Germany]], [[Hungary]], [[Netherlands]], [[Poland]], [[Slovakia]] and [[Switzerland]]. In northern Europe, in [[Denmark]], [[Ireland]], [[Sweden]] and [[United Kingdom]]. In southeastern Europe, within [[Albania]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Croatia]], [[Greece]], [[Italy]], [[Montenegro]], [[North Macedonia]], [[Romania]], [[Serbia]] and [[Slovenia]]. In southwestern Europe, it is found in [[France]], [[Portugal]] and [[Spain]].<ref name="grin"/>

It has been introduced into the American states of [[Idaho]], [[Oregon]], [[Pennsylvania]] and [[Utah]].<ref name="eflora"/><ref name="catalogueoflife">{{cite web |title=Accepted scientific name: ''Papaver argemone'' Takht. (accepted name) |url=http://www.catalogueoflife.org/col/details/species/id/32f09de383864a98276af6d5ec0b918f |publisher=catalogueoflife.org |accessdate=1 November 2017}}</ref>

===Habitat===
[[File:Papaver argemone2 eF.jpg|thumb|Seed capsule of ''Papaver argemone'']]
[[File:Papaver argemone MHNT.BOT.2016.24.41.jpg|thumb|''Papaver argemone'' - [[MHNT]]]]
It grows in fields and disturbed soils (including ploughed).<ref name=Readers/> It is normally found at {{cvt|0–300|m|ft|-2}} above sea level.<ref name="eflora"/>

==Uses==
In the past, the pale poppy was used in herbal medicines.<ref name=Readers/>

==Culture==
The petal of the poppy, was once used in folklore, as a test of faithfulness. A petal was placed in the palm of the loved ones hand and if when struck with a fist it produced a snapping sound, the loved one was true.<ref name=Readers/>
